The '''1997–98 FA Premier League''' (known as the '''FA [[Carling]] Premiership''' for sponsorship reasons) was the sixth season of the [[Premier League|FA Premier League]]. It saw [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]] lift their first league title since 1991<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.arsenal.com/first-team/honours|title=Honours|publisher=[[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]]|access-date=2 February 2020}}</ref> and, in so doing, became only the second team to win [[Double (association football)#England|The Double]] for the second time. 

It was Arsenal's first full season under French manager [[Arsène Wenger]], who became the third manager to win the Premier League. Wenger followed in the footsteps of [[Alex Ferguson]] and [[Kenny Dalglish]] and, while both Ferguson and Dalglish were [[Scotland|Scottish]], Wenger was the first manager from outside the British Isles to win a league title in England.

==Season summary==
At the end of the 1997–98 FA Premier League season, a record total of nine English teams qualified for European competition.

Premiership champions Arsenal and runners-up Manchester United qualified for the [[UEFA Champions League|Champions League]], while [[UEFA Cup]] places went to [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]], [[Leeds United F.C.|Leeds United]], [[Aston Villa F.C.|Aston Villa]] and [[Blackburn Rovers F.C.|Blackburn Rovers]]. Qualifying for the [[UEFA Cup Winners' Cup]] were [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]] (as defending champions) and FA Cup runners-up [[Newcastle United F.C.|Newcastle United]]. [[Crystal Palace F.C.|Crystal Palace]], while finishing bottom, qualified for the Intertoto Cup.<ref name="1997-98 tables">[https://www.rsssf.org/tablese/eng98.html League tables and results for English football leagues, 1997–98 season]. Retrieved 21 September 2006.</ref>

Manchester United led the table for most of the season, before a dip in form during the final two months of the campaign saw Arsenal overtake them in April, taking advantage of games in hand, and winning the league title with two away matches remaining, although the gap between the champions and runners-up was a single point in the final table as Arsenal lost their final two away fixtures and Alex Ferguson's men won both of theirs. Arsenal then completed the double by winning the FA Cup. Despite the sudden dismissal of FA Cup-winning player-manager [[Ruud Gullit]], Chelsea won the League Cup and European Cup Winners Cup under new player-manager [[Gianluca Vialli]].

The gap between the Premier League and Division One of [[the Football League]] was highlighted at the end of 1997–98 when all three newly promoted teams were relegated. [[Crystal Palace F.C.|Crystal Palace]] was confined to the bottom place in the final table, having won just two home games all season and losing most of their games in the second half of the campaign. [[Barnsley F.C.|Barnsley]]'s first season in the top division ended in relegation, although they did reach the [[FA Cup]] quarter finals and knocked out Manchester United in the Fifth Round. [[Bolton Wanderers F.C.|Bolton Wanderers]] went down on goal difference, with 17th place being occupied by Everton: despite preserving top-flight football for the 45th season running, [[Howard Kendall]] quit as manager at [[Goodison Park]] after his third spell in charge.

Another mark of the gap was that the three relegated teams in the previous season took the top three places in the [[1997–98 Football League]]. Had [[Sunderland A.F.C|Sunderland]] not lost the play-off final to [[Charlton Athletic F.C.|Charlton Athletic]] on a penalty shootout, the 20 teams from the [[1998–99 FA Premier League|1998–99 Premier League]] would have been exactly the same as those in the [[1996–97 FA Premier League|1996–97 Premier League]].

==Teams==
Twenty teams competed in the league – the top seventeen teams from the previous season and the three teams promoted from the [[1996–97 Football League First Division|First Division]]. The promoted teams were [[Bolton Wanderers F.C.|Bolton Wanderers]] (returning after a season's absence), [[Barnsley F.C.|Barnsley]] (playing in the top flight for the first time) and [[Crystal Palace F.C.|Crystal Palace]] (playing in the top flight after a two-year absence). They replaced [[Sunderland A.F.C.|Sunderland]], [[Middlesbrough F.C.|Middlesbrough]] and [[Nottingham Forest F.C.|Nottingham Forest]], who were relegated to the [[1997–98 Football League First Division|First Division]] after top flight spells of one, two and three years respectively.
